setup: Motion renders the frame at a low resolution (list.pixel: { width, height, mode }), then a scale pass draws it at the output size. In 'sharp' mode the camera snaps to the low-resolution texel grid and the residual becomes the scale pass's sub-texel offset (the shader library's sharpBilinear, web/shaders/pixel/scale.mjs).

integer.what: 160 x 90 rendered, upscaled by 6 to 960 x 540 in 'integer' mode
integer.reference: integerUpscale (web/shaders/pixel/scale.mjs) of the same low-resolution frame read back

sharp.what: the same frame in 'sharp' mode with sub-texel offsets 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75
sharp.reference: sharpBilinear of the same low-resolution frame

pan.what: a 4 x 4 texel square on a dark ground, 'sharp' mode, the camera panned in steps of 0.1 output pixels over 120 frames
pan.metric: in the output row through the square's centre, the x where the square's left edge crosses half its contrast (linear interpolation between pixel centres), against the continuous-pan position x0 - pan(t)
pan.bound: |error| <= 1 output pixel on every frame, and the edge moves monotonically (never backwards) as the camera pans one way

does_not_prove: Behaviour on content other than hard-edged squares and these frames, or on a display.
